question.problem: Compute the Wronskian $W(y_1, y_2)$ for $y_1(x) =2x$ and $y_2(x) = x^2.$
question.worked_solution:
The Wronskian $W(y_1,y_2)$ of two functions $y_1(x)$ and $y_2(x)$ is defined as

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14123785/assets/63e7eee4a168f339b9dfb1fb69ca67a3747d567020ade08c2bbab3121b530b72.svg)

In our case, we have $y_1(x) = 2x$ and $y_2(x) = x^2.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}W({y}_{1},{y}_{2}) & =2x{({x}^{2})}^{′}-{x}^{2}{(2x)}^{′} \\  & =4{x}^{2}-2{x}^{2} \\  & =2{x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
